figmaSource.structure: 12 variants cross `size` (xs/sm/md/lg, matching Avatar's own xs/sm/md/lg exactly - xxs and xl are not part of Avatar Group; default lg) x `number` (2/3/4, default 4, the count of visible avatars), plus a `showMore` boolean component property (defaultValue: true). Each variant is layoutMode HORIZONTAL with a negative itemSpacing (measured per size: xs -4, sm -4, md -8, lg -12), containing `number` `avatar` instances (each an instance-level override of the real avatar component - unmodified apart from an added separating-ring stroke, color/elevation/surface/raised/default, 1px, OUTSIDE-aligned) followed by one `dropdown-menu` instance (trigger=more-avatar, alignment=left, isOpen=false) whose trigger slot holds a `figma-parts / more-trigger` instance. That part, traced one level deeper (all 16 of its own size x state variants individually re-measured, not sampled from one), is itself a real `button` (Button) instance (appearance=subtle in code, called tone=subtle in Figma's own variant name - the same Figma-vs-code naming divergence Tag's own tone/appearance split already has) with buttonText bound to a fixed illustrative count ("+3"/"+4" depending on sample) and five instance-level overrides verified across every size/state combination: fixed square inline-size equal to its own block-size; a fully-rounded corner radius (999 on all 16); background overridden to color/elevation/surface/sunken/default - identically on all 16 variants (every size x every state, including hover/press/focus), which reads as an unfinished mockup rather than an intentional static/no-hover-feedback design, since every other interactive control in this system gives hover/press feedback; typography overridden to Body/S, M, L, L for xs/sm/md/lg (not Button's own per-size heading-based type scale - lg reuses the same Body/L style as md rather than stepping up); and padding-inline of 6/8/12/16 for xs/sm/md/lg, which for sm/md/lg happens to already equal Button's own natural per-size padding-inline default (8/12/16) - only xs (6) doesn't match Button's own default (8), and 6 isn't on the spacing scale at all. That button instance carries its own separating-ring stroke too, color/border/inverse (a different, deliberately verified token from the avatars' own ring), 1px, OUTSIDE-aligned. The nested dropdown-menu's own content slot is empty in the static file (isOpen=false, never toggled open in the source), same as Tag Group's own dropdown-menu instance.
apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's `number` (2/3/4, a fixed illustrative axis) and `showMore` (a boolean, defaultValue true) are both replaced by a single derived `hasOverflow = avatars.length > maxVisible` boolean - the same 'closed demo becomes an open, data-driven prop' adaptation Tag Group already made for its own tab-group source. A consumer cannot set showMore inconsistently with the real truncated count, since there is no separate manual toggle.

The figma-parts / more-trigger part is not implemented as a bespoke new component - it is, verified across all 16 of its own size x state variants (not sampled from one), the real Button component with instance-level overrides (forced square inline-size, fully-rounded corner radius, a sunken-surface background instead of Button's own subtle-appearance background, and Body/S-M-L-L typography instead of Button's own per-size heading-based type scale). Code reuses Button directly (appearance="subtle") and applies each override via a CSS class passed through Button's own className prop, rather than reimplementing a circular button from scratch or inventing a new Button variant.

Every one of the 16 more-trigger variants (all 4 sizes x all 4 states - default/hover/press/focus) measures the identical background fill (color/elevation/surface/sunken/default) - Figma models no visual hover/press differentiation for this part at all. Treated as an unfinished mockup rather than intentional static styling, since no other interactive control in this system omits hover/press feedback: code still differentiates hover (color/elevation/surface/sunken/hover) and press (color/elevation/surface/sunken/press) using the same token family's sibling values, which already exist for exactly this purpose.

Button's own per-size min-block-size tokens (--size-control-xs/sm/md/lg) were verified to measure identically to Avatar's own per-size tokens (--size-avatar-xs/sm/md/lg) at every one of the four shared sizes - this correspondence is what makes 'force Button's inline-size to match its own block-size' produce a circle exactly matching Avatar's own diameter, not an approximation.

The two separating-ring tokens (color-elevation-surface-raised-default around each avatar, color-border-inverse around the overflow trigger) were verified as distinct Figma variables individually, not assumed interchangeable just because both resolve to solid white in the light-mode file being inspected - using the wrong one would only surface as a visual bug in dark mode.

The overlap amount per size (xs -4, sm -4, md -8, lg -12) was measured directly rather than assumed to scale as a fixed percentage of avatar diameter (it doesn't scale perfectly - sm and xs share the same -4 value despite different diameters) - each value maps exactly onto the dedicated overlap-* semantic token family (overlap-sm/md/lg, already negative-valued), not the generic spacing-* scale, so no new token was created despite the non-uniform scaling.

maxVisible is clamped to a minimum of 1 whenever there is overflow - Figma's own component set was edited (2026-08-21) to drop its number=4 variant, leaving number=1/2/3 (each always paired with the overflow trigger, never number=0) - confirming a 'some avatars must stay visible alongside the trigger' floor is real design intent, not a code-only guess. Re-verifying the exact current number/showMore variant grid was not possible at that time - the component set was mid-edit and Figma reported 'existing errors' when reading its componentPropertyDefinitions directly (duplicate number=2 variants were found across every size). The floor behavior itself does not depend on resolving that inconsistency.

position: relative on .avatarRing and .overflowTrigger fixes a stacking-order bug verified live in a browser (not reproducible under jsdom): Avatar's own root is already position: relative, which - since neither wrapper creates its own stacking context - promotes it into .root's 'positioned' paint tier, a tier that always paints above plain static content regardless of DOM order. Button's own root is position: static, so without this the overflow trigger (last in DOM, meant to be on top) always lost to the avatar before it. Confirmed via document.elementFromPoint() at each overlap boundary both before and after the fix.

figmaSource.note: Filed on the file's own "✅⏲️ Chip" page, verified directly against the file via the Desktop Bridge plugin. The Figma build was simplified on 2026-08-27: modes renamed (filtering, property, scope) -> (filter, select, search), the `filter type` axis removed, and chip-base's mode/tone/hasValue axes dropped.
figmaSource.structure: One component set, 5 variants across two axes - `mode` (filter/select/search) and `size` (`sm (24)` / `md (32)`) - with `filter` md-only (the sm filter variants were removed): so filter/md, select/sm, select/md, search/sm, search/md. Every variant is a horizontal auto-layout row (itemSpacing 0) of segment instances that read as one pill: `mode=filter` is `figma-parts / chip-base` + one or two `dropdown-menu` instances (operator, value) + `figma-parts / remove-button`; `mode=select` is `chip-base` + `remove-button`; `mode=search` is `chip-base` alone. Outer corner radius is 999 (full round); interior corners squared. Segment corner radii measured per side: leading segment [999, 0, 0, 999], middle segments [0, 0, 0, 0], trailing segment [0, 999, 999, 0]. Measured heights match the size axis exactly (sm 24, md 32); padding-inline is 6 at sm and 8 at md, with the remove button pulled 2px toward the seam (sm 4/6, md 6/8); segment gap is 4 at both sizes. The elemBefore box hugs its content: 16px for an icon (`element=icon`) or a sm-chip avatar (`element=avatar, size=sm`), 24px for an md-chip avatar (`element=avatar, size=md`) - so the leading avatar is `xxs`/16px in a sm chip and `xs`/24px in an md chip. The value preview likewise hugs its content. The old status/context/assignee/due-date filter categories are now examples/data, not a Figma variant axis.

parts.figma-parts / chip-base: 3662:7444 - the label segment (an `elemBefore` slot plus the label text). Axes (post-simplification): size x state(default/hover/press/focus) x isSelected x isDisabled x isRemovable - the earlier mode/tone/hasValue axes were dropped.

parts.figma-parts / remove-button: 3662:25128 - a close icon in its own segment.

tokenMapping.disabled: background: color/background/disabled; text: color/content/disabled; border reverts to color/border/input

The CloseIcon inherits the remove button's colour (same :global([data-color]) inherit technique the label icon uses) rather than keeping Icon's default content/default.

apiAdaptationNotes: One `Chip` export whose props are a discriminated union on `mode`, rather than three components or one component with everything optional. This mirrors Figma's single component set while making illegal states unrepresentable - `value` cannot reach a search chip, `onSelectedChange` cannot reach a select chip.

Mode names track Figma exactly: `filter` / `select` / `search`. (Figma originally named these filtering, property, and scope; it was simplified to filter/select/search on 2026-08-27 and the code API was renamed to match.)

Figma's `filter type` axis (none/status/context/assignee/due date) is NOT modeled as a prop. Those four categories differ only in their data (icon, label, value) except for one structural fact: `due date` has an operator segment and the others do not. Code exposes that fact directly as an optional `operator` segment, so any filter can have a comparison and no fifth product category requires a code change. Figma's four types become four examples in the stories.

Figma models the operator and value as two independent `dropdown-menu` instances, each with its own `isOpen`. Code matches that exactly - each dropdown segment owns its own open state internally, so an operator menu and a value menu can never fight over one shared flag.

Chip has no `tone` axis. chip-base carried one (default/error/warning/success/information) before the simplification; every chip variant used tone=default, and the axis was since dropped from chip-base entirely. Available for a later pass if a real need appears.

chip-base's `isRemovable=false` variants exist at the part level, but no chip-level select or filter variant uses them - every verified one has a remove button. `onRemove` is therefore required for both modes rather than optional, keeping Chip distinct from Tag (which is the right component for a non-removable label).

`search` is the only mode whose label segment is itself interactive, and the only one Figma gives an unselected state, so it renders as a real toggle button carrying `aria-pressed` - the same semantics Toggle Button uses. For `filter` and `select` the label is a plain non-interactive span; only the dropdown segments and remove button are controls.

Each dropdown panel's default accessible name is composed from the property and the segment's role ("Due date operator", "Due date value") rather than the segment's own label. The segment label is the current value ("on", "March 2"), which names the panel poorly on its own. `ChipSegment.menuAriaLabel` overrides it.

Every segment except the last drops its own trailing border, so the next segment's leading border draws the seam - applied to every segment rather than only the leading one, which is what keeps the junction a uniform 1px where two middle segments meet (an operator and a value side by side, as on a due-date filter). Segment strokes are strokeAlign INSIDE at weight 1.

Figma models no selected+disabled chip-base variant at all, so disabled fully overrides selected visuals (including resetting the border to color/border/input) rather than blending the two - the same precedent Toggle Button and Toggle Icon Button already set for that gap.

chip-base has a state axis (default/hover/press/focus) in Figma, but the label segment deliberately implements no hover or press treatment in any mode - a product decision, not an oversight. In filter/select the label is a passive span that names the property; in search, selection is the feedback and the focus ring covers keyboard affordance. Interaction fills belong to the segments that act: the operator, the value, and remove. A consequence: nothing in Chip consumes --color-background-selected-default-hover/-press.
ChipSearchProps['data-force-state'] accepts only 'focus' as a result - a 'hover'/'press' value would render identically to the default and quietly mislead.

Every segment is position: relative, and the focused one gets z-index: 1. The focus ring is an outline drawn outside the segment box and segments sit flush, so without this the next segment paints over the ring's trailing edge and clips it. Same paint-tier reasoning as Avatar Group's overlapping stack, applied to an outline rather than a fill.

The remove button carries a "Remove" Tooltip on hover/focus, and Tooltip is not mounted at all while disabled. Two independent reasons point the same way: "Remove" on a chip that cannot be removed is misleading rather than explanatory (unlike IconButton disabled tooltips, which explain why an action is unavailable); and structurally, Tooltip wraps a disabled child in an extra span so pointer events still fire, which would stop the button being a direct child of the root and detach it from the pill as its own fully-rounded island - every segment rule here is structural (:first-child / :last-child / :not(:last-child)). Passing disabled to Tooltip suppresses only the popup, not the wrapper. The button own aria-label remains the accessible name, so the tooltip is never the sole one.

Each search chip is an independent on/off toggle, not a radio group - several can be on at once and Chip never coordinates siblings. Any one-of-N behaviour belongs to the consumer holding the state, the same way Toggle Button works.

size resolves as size ?? groupSize ?? md, where groupSize comes from ChipSizeContext. Chip Group provides it via context rather than by cloning children, because cloning only reaches direct children - a Chip behind a Tooltip, from a map, or behind a conditional would silently miss it. Explicit per-Chip size still wins.

figmaSource.note: Filed on the file's own "✅⏲️ Chip Group" page, verified directly against the file via the Desktop Bridge plugin.
figmaSource.structure: Four variants cross `size` (`sm (24)` / `md (32)`) with `alignment` (left/right). Every variant is a single auto-layout frame - layoutMode HORIZONTAL, layoutWrap WRAP, itemSpacing 8, counterAxisSpacing 8, counterAxisAlignItems CENTER, and zero padding - containing ten `chip` instances, all `mode=search`, `isSelected=false`, each carrying the variant's own size. `alignment=left` measures primaryAxisAlignItems MIN; `alignment=right` measures MAX. There is no overflow instance, no divider, and no container fill or stroke: the group is pure layout.
apiAdaptationNotes: Chip Group takes `children`, not a data array. Tag Group and Avatar Group own their items because they have to decide which are visible and which are truncated; Chip Group has no overflow behaviour at all, and Chip's own props are a discriminated union on `mode`, which a flat item type could not express without duplicating that union. Button Group - the closest analogue in this system - is likewise a children-based layout wrapper.

`size` reaches each Chip through React context (ChipSizeContext), not by cloning children. cloneElement only reaches direct children, so a Chip inside a Tooltip, returned from a `.map`, or rendered conditionally would silently miss the group's size - the same structural fragility that detached Chip's own remove button from its pill. Context reaches any descendant regardless of what sits between, and an explicit `size` on an individual Chip still wins because Chip resolves `size ?? groupSize ?? 'md'`.
The provider is only mounted when `size` is actually set, so a Chip Group without one leaves every Chip on its own default rather than overriding it with undefined.

`alignment` is genuinely different from Tag Group's identically-named prop despite the shared axis name. Here it maps to Figma's primaryAxisAlignItems MIN/MAX - literally which edge the chips pack against (justify-content). In Tag Group it decides where the overflow tag renders. Chip Group has no overflow, so there is nothing to place.
No overflow or truncation was implemented, because Figma models none - all ten chips in every variant are plain, equal siblings. Chip Group is deliberately not Tag Group with chips in it.

Chip Group never manages selection. Figma's variants are all `isSelected=false` search chips, and search chips are independent on/off toggles - so any one-of-N coordination belongs to the consumer holding the state, exactly as with Toggle Button.
`role="group"` is applied only when an accessible name is given (aria-label/aria-labelledby), matching Button Group - an unnamed group is a boundary a screen-reader user steps through for no benefit.

figmaLayoutData.actionButtonGroup: size=sm, shape=square, tone=default icon-buttons, cancel/close first then confirm/check, confirmed via screenshot of the state=edit variant

apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's 'state' axis (default/edit) is not implemented as a state or isEditing prop at all - editing state and the in-progress draft are owned entirely inside the component. Two earlier passes exposed isEditing externally (first fully controlled by the parent, then still controlled but toggleable); both were reverted after explicit design feedback that no real use case shows the confirm/cancel buttons before the field has been interacted with - editing must always start on click/focus.

state=default renders nothing but an empty slot - no read-only text, no pencil/edit icon, confirmed via screenshot. Rather than invent a separate read-mode display, Inline Edit clones the SAME single children element for both states via React.cloneElement (readOnly+value when not editing, draft+onChange when editing) - the same DOM node persists across the transition, so focus is never lost when editing starts on focus.

value/onConfirm mirror TextField's own controlled value pattern: the parent supplies the last confirmed value and receives it back via onConfirm only on commit, not per keystroke. Cancel discards the draft and reverts to value, calling onCancel with no value argument (the parent already has it).

Enter-to-confirm and Escape-to-cancel are an explicit addition beyond the two visible icon buttons Figma shows, confirmed as wanted by the user. Enter also calls preventDefault so a nested control inside a native <form> doesn't trigger an accidental submission. Both keys blur the field afterward (deselecting it), matching what clicking either action button already does - the same mousedown-set ref flag the action buttons use suppresses handleBlur's auto-confirm from re-firing off this same-tick blur.

children is expected to be a single controlled input-like element (TextField today, typically appearance=subtle so it reads as plain text at rest) rather than two separate read/edit elements the parent swaps between.

Figma's literal state=edit layout puts the action buttons trailing in the same row as the field, which would force the field to shrink to make room once editing starts. Per explicit design feedback, this implementation stacks the action row below the field instead (flex-direction: column, 8px gap, action row align-self: flex-end to anchor to the trailing/right edge) so the field keeps its full width in both states.

The picker's own anatomy was built from the `type-cursor` figma-part added to text-field on 2026-08-28 (open-search / type-to-search variants) fed into a dropdown-menu variant with a defined open menu. Because the mode is behavior, not appearance, most of this component has no static Figma counterpart to verify against.
figmaSource.structure: The editor frame is Text Area's frame, token-for-token. The `/` mini-input reuses Text Field's look (background, input border, radius) at a small size, per the Figma type-cursor part. The picker is the menu organism with search hidden - the query is typed inline in the editor, not in the panel - with one section per entity type and a 16px IconTile heading.
apiAdaptationNotes: Built as a separate `RichTextArea` component rather than a `type` prop on TextArea. The two share a frame but nothing else: one is a native <textarea> with a string value, the other is a contenteditable surface with a structured node array, `onSearch`, and an entity config. A single component would have had two disjoint prop sets and two disjoint values.

The value is a flat node array (`RichTextValue`) - runs of text interleaved with entity nodes - not HTML or Markdown. It is what you persist; serialize it however your store needs. Storing HTML would leak the editor's DOM shape into consumers' data.

Hydrates from `value` once, then runs uncontrolled - the DOM is the source of truth while editing, with `onChange` reporting each serialized change. A contenteditable surface cannot be re-rendered from props on every keystroke without destroying the caret.

The `/` query lives in an inline editable span inside the editor (the Figma `type-cursor` look), so the picker panel has no search field of its own - `showSearch={false}`. This matches Figma and mirrors how Select types in the trigger while the panel only lists options.

Focus stays in the editor while the picker is open; the keyboard-active row is marked with a class rather than by moving focus, so typing continues to land in the `/` span. See knownLimitations for the accessibility consequence.

Each tag is a non-editable host span with a `NavTag` portaled into it. contenteditable would otherwise let the caret walk into the tag's internals; a host span keeps each tag atomic to the caret while still being a real React subtree.
`NavTag` is a preset over the Tag atom, not a new component - Tag already does tone (color), `elemBefore` (icon), and `href` (navigation). An entityType only needs to resolve to a tone plus an icon.
Non-empty queries are debounced 150ms; an empty query resolves immediately from `recents` (or `onSearch('')`) so opening the picker feels instant.
`scrollIntoView` on the active row is called optionally - jsdom does not implement it, and an unguarded call throws inside any consumer's test.

figmaSource.structure: One component set, 84 variants across six axes - size (sm/md/lg), tone (default/subtle), state (default/hover/focus/typing/hasValue), inputType (single/multi), isInvalid, isDisabled. Every variant is a `dropdown-menu` instance (Popup + panel) whose trigger slot holds a `figma-parts / select-trigger` (4658:67775), which is itself a `text-field` instance carrying a trailing `caret_down` in its elemAfterInput slot. In multi + hasValue, the trigger's text-field also holds `chip-container` frames (chip-base, mode=select) ahead of the input. The panel's surface slot is the generic empty `panelSurface` in the static file - the real option list is a code decision, the same 'static mockup, real content is code' pattern as every other dropdown-menu-based molecule. Trigger geometry measured per size: sm 32 / radius 8, md 40 / radius 8, lg 48 / radius 12; frame fill color/elevation/surface/raised/default (hover raised/hover), border color/border/input, focus+typing border color/border/focused, disabled background/disabled + border/disabled. The multi trigger is single-line, NO_WRAP at every size - chips sit inline, chip size sm for sm/md triggers and md for lg.

parts.figma-parts / select-trigger: 4658:67775 - 84 variants mirroring select's own axes. Structurally a text-field instance + trailing caret, so the code trigger is the existing TextField molecule, not a bespoke frame.
parts.text-field: The trigger's frame, fill, border, focus/invalid/disabled treatment and per-size geometry are exactly the TextField molecule's - verified token-for-token, so Select reuses TextField rather than restating its state CSS.
parts.caret_down: icon 1496:1775 = the codebase's CaretDownIcon, in the trigger's elemAfterInput slot.
parts.chip-base: multi-select values render as Chips (mode="select") inside the trigger.

apiAdaptationNotes: Props are a discriminated union on `inputType` (default 'single'), so single-select's scalar `value: string | null` and multi-select's `value: string[]` cannot be mixed up - the same pattern Chip uses for `mode`. Single's onChange takes `string | null`; multi's takes `string[]`.

Options are a flat `SelectOption[]` ({ value, label, icon?, description?, disabled?, group? }), not Menu's `MenuSection[]`. Select maps them into sections itself - grouping consecutive options by their `group` field - and owns each row's selected state, selectionType (radio for single, checkbox for multi), and onSelect. This is the ergonomic shape a Select consumer expects; the caller never hand-wires Menu rows.

The trigger is the existing TextField molecule. TextField needed one additive extension - a `leadingContent` slot rendered inside the frame, before the input, NOT aria-hidden (unlike the decorative `iconBefore`) - so multi-select chips render inside the field without a second bordered frame or restating TextField's state CSS. The slot shrinks and clips to keep the field single-line, matching Figma's NO_WRAP trigger. Same 'extend the atom to fill a composition gap' move as Tag's isInteractive and Avatar's entityType.
tone maps to TextField's `appearance` (default/subtle) - Figma names the axis `tone` on the trigger, but it is TextField's appearance axis, so code uses TextField's own name at that boundary.

A11y is the menu pattern, not the strict ARIA combobox/listbox pattern - a deliberate choice matching Figma's own composition (a text input + a dropdown-menu). The input is role=combobox with aria-haspopup=menu and aria-autocomplete=list; the panel is Menu's role=menu with menuitemradio (single) / menuitemcheckbox (multi) rows. Opening keeps focus in the input; ArrowDown moves focus into the Menu, whose existing roving-tabindex takes over; Escape/outside-click close and return focus to the input. A strict listbox (role=listbox/option + aria-activedescendant, focus staying in the input) would not reuse Menu at all and would diverge from how Figma composed it.

Typeahead filtering is Select's own (case-insensitive substring on label) and passed to Menu as pre-filtered sections with showSearch=false - the user chose the trigger itself as the search field over Menu's own built-in search box. A controlled searchValue + onSearchChange hands filtering to the caller (e.g. async loading), in which case Select stops filtering internally.

Multi-select values are removable two ways, matching the confirmed product intent: an ✕ on each Chip (Chip mode=select's own remove button) and re-picking the row in the open menu (checkbox toggles off). Backspace on an empty query removes the last chip. Figma's chip-base shows isRemovable=false, but that is the static mockup state.

The panel always matches the field frame's width and left edge. The trigger child that carries the merged ref + aria-expanded/aria-controls is the inset input (where that a11y wiring belongs), but Select also passes the field frame (the input's parentElement, via a callback ref) as Dropdown Menu's `anchorRef` and sets `matchTriggerWidth`. Popup then measures, positions, width-matches, and scopes its outside-click boundary to the frame - not the ~9px-inset input - and the inner Menu fills that width via `fullWidth`. This keeps the input's single-child trigger + a11y contract intact while the dropdown lines up flush with the visible control. Verified live: panel width and left both equal the frame's on single and multi.
`inputType` is not offered as a runtime-mixable prop; a Select is single or multi for its lifetime, as its value type differs. This mirrors Chip's mode union.

figmaSource.structure: 24 variants cross `tone` (default/primary - code calls this `appearance`) x `size` (xs/sm/md/lg, matching Button's own four sizes exactly) x `isDisabled` x `isOpen`, with isOpen never crossed with isDisabled=true (8 tone x size combinations x 3 states [isDisabled=false+isOpen=false, isDisabled=false+isOpen=true, isDisabled=true] = 24). Each variant is layoutMode HORIZONTAL, itemSpacing 0, containing: a real `button` (Button) instance whose trailing corners are squared to 0 (leading corners keep Button's own per-size radius - measured topLeft/bottomLeft: 12, topRight/bottomRight: 0 at size=lg) AND whose trailing-edge stroke is individually zeroed (measured strokeTopWeight/strokeBottomWeight/strokeLeftWeight: 1, strokeRightWeight: 0); a `figma-parts / split-button / divider` instance (a single 1px VECTOR, height matching the button, fill color keyed to tone); and a `popup` instance (alignment="bottom right") whose trigger slot holds a `figma-parts / secondary-action` instance - traced one level deeper, a real `icon-button` (IconButton) instance (shape=square) with a single `caret_down` icon child, whose leading corners are squared to 0 (trailing corners keep IconButton's own radius, the exact mirror of the primary action) AND whose leading-edge stroke is individually zeroed (measured strokeLeftWeight: 0, the exact mirror of the primary action's strokeRightWeight: 0). The popup's own surface slot holds the generic `figma-parts/panelSurface` with an empty content slot in the static file (isOpen=false examples) or also empty even where isOpen=true (same 'static mockup, real content is a code decision' pattern as Tag Group/Avatar Group's own dropdown-menu instances).
apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's own reference instance for the open panel is a raw `popup` instance, not a `dropdown-menu` instance - but the panel's real purpose ("choose from a small group of similar actions", per the component's own Figma description) is exactly Dropdown Menu's established use case. Code reuses Dropdown Menu directly (children=the secondary-action IconButton, sections=the small group of actions) rather than hand-assembling Popup and Menu a second time, matching Tag Group/Avatar Group's own precedent rather than literally mirroring this one instance's authoring shortcut.

appearance is deliberately narrower than Button's own (`'default' | 'primary'` only, omitting `'subtle'`) - every one of the 24 verified split-button variants uses only default/primary; Figma never shows a subtle split button, so code doesn't invent one.

secondaryActionLabel is a required prop, not auto-derived from the primary action's own label - the caret segment has no visible text to derive a name from, and an auto-generated label (e.g. `${children} options`) could read oddly for non-string labels.

The figma-parts / split-button / divider part is not implemented as a new exported primitive - it's namespaced as component-specific in Figma (unlike figma-parts / secondary-action, which is reused across other components), and no existing shared Divider component exists in this codebase to reuse instead. Implemented as a single internal <span>.

IconButton's own isExpanded prop is not passed to the secondary action - verified directly in code that it only sets aria-expanded/data-expanded with no corresponding CSS (no visual effect today), and Popup (via Dropdown Menu) already overwrites aria-expanded via its own trigger-cloning regardless of whatever IconButton would set internally.

Verified directly that IconButton's own tooltip-auto-wrapping (triggered by passing an explicit aria-label, IconButton's own pre-existing behavior unrelated to Split Button) does not interfere with the outer Popup's (Dropdown Menu's) own trigger-cloning - ref and aria-expanded/aria-controls are injected as props on the authored <IconButton> element itself and correctly routed to its real internal <button> via IconButton's own forwardRef and prop-destructuring, regardless of what IconButton renders around it internally. This exact combination already exists, unremarked, in Dropdown Menu's own Content story.

alignment is hardcoded to 'right' on the internal DropdownMenu call, not exposed as a SplitButtonProps prop - Figma's own split-button variant set has no alignment axis at all; every one of the 24 variants opens "bottom right". This is a preferred alignment only, not a forced one - it maps to Popup's own 'bottomRight' (via Dropdown Menu's ALIGNMENT_MAP), and Popup's own collision detection already flips to an alternate alignment (then clamps to the viewport) when there isn't room, with no extra logic needed in Split Button.
isFullWidth is omitted from the Button props Split Button inherits (Omit<ButtonProps, 'appearance' | 'isFullWidth'>) - no verified Figma variant for a full-width split button exists.

Each segment suppresses its own border on the interior edge (border-inline-end-width: 0 on .primaryAction, border-inline-start-width: 0 on .secondaryAction) - Figma's own button/icon-button instances measure strokeRightWeight/strokeLeftWeight: 0 on that exact edge, so the divider is the only thing drawing that seam. Caught live in Storybook: without this, Button's/IconButton's own 1px border on that edge stacked with the 1px divider into a visibly wide line instead of one clean 1px seam.

IconButton's own appearance_primary:disabled (and appearance_subtle:disabled) was fixed to stay borderless (border-color: transparent), matching Button's own disabled rule split and Figma's own disabled variants (identical fill regardless of tone, but primary/subtle drop the stroke entirely - verified directly against Figma's disabled component variants). It previously shared the same visible-border rule as appearance_default:disabled, so a disabled primary secondary action looked identical to a disabled default one. This is an IconButton-atom fix (icon-button.module.css), not Split-Button-specific, but Split Button's primary+disabled secondary action is what surfaced it.

The primary-appearance divider's fill is bound to a Figma variable named color/border/brand/primary/subtle. That token now exists code-side (added in the brand-taupe token migration): prussian-300 in light, prussian-900 in dark - the exact Figma-matching token, now used for this divider. Its obvious-looking non-subtle sibling color-border-brand-primary-default does not work here - it resolves to the same prussian-900 primitive as the primary button's own background (color-background-brand-primary-bold-default), so a divider painted in it disappears against an identical-colored surface. Resolving Figma's fill node directly (not just the variable name) gives prussian-300, a light tint, not a darker/duller shade of prussian-900. Before the migration the divider used color-content-brand-primary-subtle as a stand-in - identical in light (prussian-300) but prussian-700 rather than prussian-900 in dark; it now uses color-border-brand-primary-subtle, reused here on a background-color the same way Slider's own active track-stop dot already reuses it for contrast against a bold fill (see slider.module.css's own comment). Caught live in Storybook twice: first the mistyped -subtle name resolved to nothing (fully transparent); after that fix, the syntactically-valid color-border-brand-primary substitute was present but exactly camouflaged against both buttons' own background.

figmaSource.note: The real Figma component set is named tab-group, not tag-group - a naming typo, verified directly against the file via the Desktop Bridge plugin. It is filed on the file's own "✅ Tag Group" page, and every variant is unambiguously a wrapping row of `tag` instances plus an eleventh `tag` (reading "+5 more") nested inside a `dropdown-menu` instance's trigger slot - not tabs. Code follows the real, verified structure under the correct name, TagGroup.
figmaSource.structure: Four variants cross two axes: `size` (`sm (24)` / `md (32)`) x `alignment`. Each variant is an auto-layout frame (layoutWrap: WRAP, itemSpacing: 8, counterAxisSpacing: 8, counterAxisAlignItems: CENTER) containing ten `tag` instances (tone=standard/default, isRemovable=false, elemBefore=false, text "Tag") plus one `dropdown-menu` instance (trigger=tag, alignment=left, isOpen=false) whose trigger slot holds an eleventh `tag` instance reading "+5 more" (same variant shape as the others: tone=standard, isRemovable=false). Every `tag` instance inside a variant - the ten visible ones and the overflow trigger's - carries that variant's own size, so size is uniform per group with no per-tag mixing. Measured frame heights match the size axis exactly (sm: 24, md: 32). In `alignment=left`, the dropdown-menu instance is the last child (trailing); in `alignment=right`, it is the first child (leading). The nested dropdown-menu's own `alignment` property measures `left` in every case - it does not flip with the outer variant.
apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's example is a fixed illustrative count (10 visible tags + a "+5 more" overflow tag = 15 total, with no exposed count/list-editing property). Code generalizes this into an open, data-driven `tags: TagGroupItem[]` array plus a `maxVisible` number, the same 'closed demo becomes an open prop' adaptation Menu made for its own `sections` versus Figma's per-variant row instances.

Figma's `alignment` variant (left/right) became TagGroupProps.alignment directly, unchanged in name or values - it controls only where the overflow tag renders (trailing vs. leading), not which tags are visible or truncated, matching the fact that every Figma variant shows the identical placeholder tag set.

Figma's `size` axis (`sm (24)` / `md (32)`) became TagGroupProps.size, carrying Tag's own TagSize values (sm/md) rather than Figma's parenthesised pixel labels. It applies uniformly to every visible tag and to the overflow tag, because that is what Figma does inside each variant - so TagGroupItem omits `size` from Tag's own props entirely. TagGroup defaults to `sm`, a deliberate divergence from Tag's own `md` code default: `size=sm (24)` is the first variant in Figma's grid and the one its illustrative examples use.

The nested dropdown-menu's own `alignment` property was measured as `left` in both outer `alignment` variants (not flipped for `alignment=right`) - code matches this directly: TagGroup always renders the overflow tag's DropdownMenu with Dropdown Menu's own default alignment (left), rather than deriving or flipping it from TagGroup's own `alignment` prop.

The overflow tag's trigger needed a plain, focusable, non-navigational, non-removable interactive form - a gap in Tag's own code API (Tag was previously focusable only via `href` or its remove button). Added `isInteractive` to Tag itself (see tag.contract.json's own apiAdaptationNotes) rather than reimplementing a one-off interactive wrapper inside Tag Group.

Figma's nested `dropdown-menu` instance has an empty `content` slot in the static file (isOpen=false, never toggled open in the source), so the overflow panel's actual content (a Menu row per truncated tag) is a code-level design decision, not something measured from an open Figma variant - informed directly by Dropdown Menu's own established 'always renders a Menu built from sections' rule.

The `sm` size was removed on 2026-08-27 (it read almost identically to md); the size axis is now md/lg. variantCount reflects that removal (was 96) and should be re-confirmed live next time the Components file is connected.

Each variant is a single `Container` frame holding the text; the visual frame (fill, border, radius) is bound on the component node, not the inner Container (which carries only padding). Geometry measured per size: padding block/inline md 8/8, lg 12/12; radius lg (8) at md, xl (12) at lg; font body-md (14/24) at md, body-lg (16/24) at lg. State frame tokens (tone=default): default fill background/input/default + border/input 1px; hover fill background/input/hovered; focus fill background/input/pressed + border/focused 2px; typing border/focused 2px; filled + autofill = default; invalid border/error 2px; disabled background/disabled + border/disabled. tone=subtle has a transparent box with a bottom-only accent that reveals on hover (border/input) / focus (border/focused) / invalid (border/error), bottom corners square.
apiAdaptationNotes: Renders the frame styling directly on the <textarea> (no wrapper element), because Text Area - unlike Text Field - has no leading/trailing icon slots to compose around the control. This also lets the browser's native resize grip work with no extra wiring.
Figma's `tone` axis is exposed in code as `appearance` (default/subtle) - the same axis and the same name its sibling Text Field uses, so the two components share one vocabulary.

Figma binds a newer `background/input/*` + `border/focused` token naming that has no counterpart in this build. Those map one-to-one onto the `elevation/surface/raised/*` + `border/focus` semantic tokens Text Field already consumes (same intent), so Text Area reuses those rather than inventing unbacked tokens - keeping it visually identical to Text Field per token governance's reuse-first rule.

Focus and invalid replace the border color and paint the extra pixel via an inset box-shadow rather than a real 1px->2px border-width change - the same technique Text Field uses, so the multi-line text never shifts by a pixel on focus/blur or invalid toggle.

Figma tints the fill on focus (`background/input/pressed`); code deliberately keeps the resting fill on focus instead, matching Text Field's established no-tint-on-focus behavior (and that token does not exist here).

The `state` axis (hover/focus/typing/filled/autofill) is not a prop - those are live pseudo-classes (`:hover`, `:focus`), with a documentation-only `data-force-state` pin mirroring them for static Storybook reference, exactly as Text Field, Button, and Checkbox do. `filled`, `typing`, and `autofill` need no distinct styling (they render as default/focus).

The `type=rich-inline` variant is implemented as a separate component, `RichTextArea` (molecules/text-area/rich). It is an inline entity-tagging mode - visually identical to `default`, the difference is entirely behavioral: `/` opens a grouped entity picker and each choice is inserted inline as a navigational tag. It is separate rather than a `type` prop because its value (a structured node array), its callbacks (`onSearch`), and its surface (contenteditable) are all disjoint from the plain <textarea>. TextArea therefore still exposes no `type` prop; reach for RichTextArea instead.

Adds a `resize` prop (none/vertical/horizontal/both, default vertical) mapping to the CSS `resize` property - not a Figma axis, but the standard, expected control for a text area. A disabled field locks resize to none.

The icon-button case uses appearance=subtle, shape=square. A third `label` type was added later, nesting a real Label atom instance (tone=default, emphasis=subtle) for compact metadata/status after the input (e.g. a unit or status pill) - confirmed directly from the component's own nested instance properties, not assumed. iconAfter is already typed React.ReactNode and .action is a plain centered flex wrapper, so a Label already renders correctly there with no component code changes.

apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's 'state' axis (default/hover/focus/typing/filled) is not a real prop - verified from bound tokens: hover=:hover, focus=focus+empty (:focus-within + :placeholder-shown), typing=focus+has-value (:focus-within, not :placeholder-shown), filled=unfocused+has-value (not :placeholder-shown). All four derive from native pseudo-classes plus the input's own value; none are exposed as a prop.

Figma's 'tone' axis (standard/subtle) is renamed to 'appearance' (default/subtle) - a pure visual-weight distinction, matching this system's existing appearance vocabulary (see Button) rather than the semantic-meaning 'tone' word.
isInvalid renders with strokeWeight=2 even when not focused, confirmed directly from node data - invalid's thicker border is not a focus-only effect.

Figma's literal focus treatment thickens the frame's own border 1px->2px and swaps its color to --color-border-focus. Focus/typing replaces the resting border's color directly - the same pattern invalid already uses - rather than adding an outline ring around it, per explicit design feedback. Border width does not literally change to 2px, though: an earlier pass changed the real border-width on appearance=default's focus AND invalid, matching Figma directly, but that shifts the content box (and the placeholder/value text and typing caret) on every side, reported directly against the component from a side-by-side screenshot - both now paint the extra pixel via box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px <color> instead, keeping border-width a constant 1px in the box model with zero layout impact.

Hover is suppressed once the field is focus/typing (:focus-within, or the pinned data-force-state='focus' reference) - hover should only ever be visible on an inactive field, per explicit design feedback.

showCaret and placeholder (BOOLEAN) component properties exist only to drive Figma's own mockup and have no code equivalent - a real input shows its own caret and switches placeholder/value automatically.

appearance=subtle's bottom corners are always square (border-bottom-{left,right}-radius: 0), confirmed directly from Figma's per-corner radius data on the subtle variants - only the top corners share appearance=default's radius.

appearance=subtle rests at the same 1px bottom border-width appearance=default uses at rest, per explicit design feedback (an earlier pass reserved a constant 2px transparent border specifically to avoid a layout shift; that reservation was reverted). Reverting it reintroduced the shift a real border-width change causes (the vertically-centered text visibly nudges by a pixel), so focus/invalid on appearance=subtle now paint the thicker look via box-shadow (inset 0 -1px 0 0 <color>) instead, keeping border-bottom-width a constant 1px in the box model at every state - zero layout impact. appearance.default's own invalid/focus still uses a real border-width change (a whole-box change on all four sides is a much smaller relative shift there), so this technique is specific to appearance=subtle.

`.root[data-invalid='true']` sets the border-width shorthand (all four sides) to 2px; `.appearance_subtle[data-invalid='true']` overrides border-top/right/left-width back to 0 and must also explicitly reset border-bottom-width back to 1px, or that side silently inherits the shorthand's leftover 2px and reintroduces the same text shift.

Hovering an invalid appearance=subtle field keeps the error border color rather than resetting to --color-border-input, per explicit design feedback - the border-color-changing hover rule is scoped with :not([data-invalid='true']); the background-changing hover rule is not, since hover should still tint the background on an invalid field.

elemBeforeInput and elemAfterInput are separate, asymmetric Figma components (icon|text vs icon-button|button), not a symmetric before/after pair - iconBefore is always aria-hidden, iconAfter is never forced aria-hidden.
Inline padding is asymmetric per size (tighter on the end side) and the icon/input gap varies per size (4px/6px/8px) rather than a flat 6px, confirmed directly from Figma's per-side bound variables.

elemAfterInput gained a third `type` option in Figma - `label` - alongside `icon` and `button`, nesting a real Label atom instance (tone=default, emphasis=subtle, size sm/md). Since `iconAfter` is already `React.ReactNode` and `.action` is a plain centered flex wrapper, this required no component code change - only documenting the newly-supported content type.

Gained an additive leadingContent slot so Select can render multi-select chips inside the field frame without a second bordered frame or duplicated state CSS. In-frame, before the input, not aria-hidden (unlike the decorative iconBefore); shrinks/clips to keep the field single-line. Additive and opt-in - existing TextField usage is unchanged. Not derived from a TextField Figma variant; it exists to serve Select, whose own select-trigger nests chips inside its text-field instance.

It was previously asymmetric (4px top / 8px bottom); the bottom was tightened to 4px in Figma, so code collapsed the two longhands into one `padding-block`. Direct inspection of the actual instance (not just its component-property defaults) confirmed `elemAfterInput` (the clear icon-button) is used, but no leading `elemBeforeInput` icon - the search field has no leading icon at all. The outer `code-parts / <menu-search>` wrapper itself only has default/focus/typing variants - no hover variant at all - and the nested text-field instance's own `fills`/`strokes` are empty ([]) in every one of those three states. Code therefore neutralizes TextField's own `appearance="subtle"` hover-background and focus-underline rules specifically inside Menu's `.search` wrapper (a local-class-plus-global-attribute-selector override, no `!important`) rather than relying on `appearance="subtle"` alone, which still shows both. apiAdaptationNotes: Figma models menu-item content as free-floating slots inside a component-set variant grid (state x isSelected x isDisabled), not a data structure. Code inverts this into a `sections: MenuSection[]` prop - each item a plain object (`MenuItem`) - so a real list of N items doesn't require N manually-composed component instances.

leadingElement/trailingElement are typed as arbitrary React.ReactNode but are documented as decorative-only in code: a real interactive Checkbox/Radio/Button nested inside the row's own <button> would be invalid HTML. This matches Figma exactly, not just a code-side precaution - the file's own 'checkboxes'/'radios' slot-content demos (menu-item Parts group) swap elemBefore's nested icon INSTANCE_SWAP property to the icon components `checkbox_fill`/`checkbox-empty`/`radio_checked`/`radio_unchecked` (colored `color/content/brand/primary/default` when checked, `color/content/subtle` when not - i.e. IconColor `brand`/`subtle`), never to a real Checkbox/Radio component. Selection semantics are carried by the row's own `selected`/`selectionType`, not by whatever's rendered in the slot. Every elemBefore icon (including plain, non-selectable action rows) uses the icon wrapper's `Size: md` + `spacing: spacious (24px)` component properties - code maps this to Icon's `spacing="spacious"` (size="md" is already Icon's own default).

selectionType ('checkbox' | 'radio') is a code-level addition with no direct Figma component property - inferred from the same 'checkboxes'/'radios' slot-content demos above, which show real-world compositions where isSelected pairs with a checkbox/radio-shaped row. Modeled per-item rather than as a menu-level 'selectionMode' so a single menu can mix plain action rows with a selectable group.

Arrow-key roving-tabindex navigation (ArrowUp/Down/Home/End) has no Figma variant at all - it's a code-level accessibility decision for the ARIA menu pattern, delivering on Popup's own contract.json futureEnhancements note ('a documented recipe for wiring keyboard arrow navigation once Dropdown Menu exists').

The leading visual is an IconTile (Figma appearance=blue/green/... maps to IconTile tone); loading shows a Spinner. Toasts are shown/stacked by ToastGroup.
